comment: Dr. Cooper has some bad rep but I really enjoyed her teaching style. She is willing to help, and is always transparent with you. Due to having many classes, she will recommend you get a tutor, but that means ONE ON ONE help so it's nice. If you study regularly, are attentive, and do all the work you will be fine.

She is recently getting a bad rep. Yes, this class is hard if you don't have it in you to study a lot during the week but I think an A is very achievable for everyone which is why I still think shes a great option and a lot nicer than gets credit for.

If you were good at Calc in HS and were just too lazy to try on the AP exam, the class is designed to be a cakewalk. If you weren't great or are rusty, you will drown if you fall behind at any point or struggle with a concept due to the test/quiz system. Otherwise, Caring and Helpful Professor, would stay away if you aren't strictly reviewing.

While I do think Cooper is a genuinely good and caring professor, her lessons and coursework are far too confusing. She switches from lecturing to not teaching us at all in a single class, the grading scale is also way too confusing, and her absence policy is unforgiving. She's fine if you need a gen ed but stay away if you're majoring in math.

I loved Dr. Cooper! If you're not strong in algebra, this class can be tough. I think the reality is people who don't do well in this class weren't ready for this level of math, UR should offer lower-level math options. More profs than Dr. C do "mastery-based," it's hard to escape. There's lots of TA help - pay attention, study, and you'll do well.

Honestly she is one of the hardest reads on a person in my whole life. She's so nice but so mean. Her classes are so hard and boring but also extremely easy. There's no wonder her ratings are all 5s or 1s, you either hate her or you love her. Her mastery based system is weird, and creates lots of stress towards the end of the year.

This is the absolute worst professor I have ever had. She is rude during class and extremely unwelcoming to feedback. Her grading system makes it difficult to succeed, as she does not care if you know calculus, she only cares about if you know HER way of doing calculus. Do not take this class.
Take any professor But Dr. Cooper. You don't learn, lectures are not good. Very nit picky with everything. Not pleasant. Don't do it unless you have to for math credit.

"Taught," or more accurately, breezed over large quantities of material in a lecture-heavy environment and then expected near perfection on the following "checkpoint" or test, which is every other week. Test questions were always more difficult, and I found myself re-teaching the material often. Felt like I was drowning, not very understanding. RUN

Dr. Cooper is a horrible professor. It's an embarrassment that she does not provide any sort of reliable communication to her students. I've never heard of a professor saying that they don't look at their email. Had two office hours that were for all of her classes. Do not take her. The University should be ashamed.
The worst professor I've ever had.

Her mastery grading system makes getting an A pretty difficult to do. You have 42 learning points you can get and must get at least 39 for an A. If you get 38, you get a B, not even an A-. If you take Dr. Cooper, be ready for her to fly through the material and not even use the textbook. She is better for Calc 1 than for Calc 2. What an experience.

The grade is heavily dependent on earning 44 points out of a total of 48 on tests in order to get an A. You can earn a max of 2 points on each topic question. If you earn even 1 less point, you get a B. Not even an A-. This puts a lot of pressure on you if you don't earn enough points at the start. Outside that, just do ur work on time and ur fine.

Fairly tough grader since she utilizes a mastery grading system so there is no partial credit. However, she is always open to feedback about the course and if you need extensions or express concerns, she's sooo understanding. Heavily lecture based but the homework isn't too bad and you get a notecard for exams. I would recommend for calc 1!

What a complete joke of a class. Barely teaches- doesn't use the book you buy and gets her questions from AI.  Makes constant mistakes and has the audacity to use a mastery x2 based system. you need to get the problem correct twice before it actually counts for credit.  office hours are horrendous bc of all the students there lined up for help- RUN

For the most part, Dr. Cooper's class wasn't bad. If you put the time into understanding the material you should get an A. If Calculus doesn't come naturally to you, it might be a little bit harder because she moves quickly, but it is still manageable. One downside is that Dr. Cooper doesn't respond quickly outside of class, so be ready to wait.

This Dr. Cooper is not the Dr. Cooper I heard about. Her "mastery system" reinforces last-minute studying. 
Grading sucks. Her "revolutionary" system determines your grade based on quiz points. 39 points = A. 38 points = B. 1 single quiz question can be the difference. 

PS: good luck getting an email back! She goes AWOL outside of lecture.
tough lectures to follow and comes off aggressive, never responds to emails, checkpoints were very difficult.

I do not recommend Dr. Cooper at all.  Get mastery based system is beyond confusing and makes it almost impossible to get an A.  She does not respond to any emails and is so unhelpful when you come to her with any questions or concerns.  Choose someone else for Calc.

Honestly this mastery system is terrible. Questions take so long on tests you can never attempt all or even most of them. Grade is soley based on the tests. Journals are on rolling basis throughout the semester but quite difficult so start very early. NEVERRR answers emails, nor is avaliable. Teaching style is okay.

Save your GPA and avoid Dr. Cooper. Her new mastery based system is extremely confusing and unfair. The tests are extremely difficult and your test grades are the ONLY thing that determine your letter grade. So if you don't ace your tests, good luck even getting a B-. Her lectures and office hours are unhelpful and she never answers emails.

This class is no longer an easy A so scrap all the previous reviews. Because of reviews telling her that the class was easy she has made this class INSANELY difficult. Please avoid taking Dr. Cooper. Her grading system is so difficult and is extremely unhelpful and inaccessible outside of class. Even the hardest workers in the class have a C.

If you want an A, DO NOT take Dr Cooper. Her grading system makes it so your entire grade is reliant on tough tests, she never answers emails, comes off as aggressive, makes journals and tests inexplicably difficult, and assigns SO much work. Past reviews were positive, but her grading system has changed. Choose another professor if you can.

Dr. Cooper's mastery-based grading system is overwhelming and confusing. She is rarely available to meet, making it difficult to get help or clarification. The lack of clarity, structure, and support adds unnecessary stress. Her exams are extremely difficult, and she does not effectively teach the material, leaving students feeling unprepared .

The checkpoints were extremely challenging, with single questions taking upwards of 45 minutes. Her lectures were a bunch of definitions with examples, making it very hard to actually understand the concepts and apply them to the complex questions we got assessed on. I think she is steering this course away from its reputation as an easy A.

Professor Cooper wants her students to succeed and get good grades - she does no grading grading system (you just have to take a question per each unit on the test and once you pass all of them you don't have to take the final). She provides good videos before her lectures and gives many mental health days. Easy A in calc with minimal work
You get an easy A and learn almost nothing.

Cares so much about her students and genuinely wants you to succeed. Will always do what she can to help you. Pretty easy class but this was a lower-level class. Def recommend her. Also she is just a great person and has a good teaching style. Mastery based grading system def takes weight off your shoulders and helps u focus on ur work not grade

Dr. Cooper is by far the best professor I've had at UR. She breaks down concepts to ensure everyone from all levels of mathematics can understand. I highly recommend any of her classes, but they fill up fast. 
-Uses mastery-based grading system
-Has mental-health days built into class schedule

Dr. Cooper wants you to get an A, and almost the entire class receives one. She uses a mastery-based learning system, which makes difficult topics simple. I believe this was her first time teaching Calc III at Richmond, as she was more organized when I took her for Calc II. With that said, you should take her for Calc III or any math class at UR.
Dr. Cooper is the goat. Love her mastery system, super easy way to learn calc, and she really cares about her students. I waited a semester to take her and it was easily worth it
Dr. Cooper is by far the best professor I've had on campus and really cares about her students. She made a boring subject interesting.

If you can, take Dr. Cooper for Calculus. The Learning Target grading system is confusing at first but makes getting an A easy and assessments low stakes. Dr. Cooper is also highly caring; she will cancel class as a "mental health day" if students seem stressed.

Dr. Cooper is a super cool math prof who's very passionate about what she does. Her lectures were easy to follow, and I appreciated her mastery-based grading system. The 3 journal essays she has you write are kind of a waste of time, but other than that, she's fantastic, and it's not hard to do well in her class. Take her for Calc 2 if you can.

The mastery-based grading system was just one example of the care that Dr. Cooper has for her students. She truly cares deeply about all of them, and it shows. She also is obviously very passionate about mathematics, and it was inspiring, at least to me. One downside is that she wasn't very good at sticking to her schedule on the syllabus

Calc 1 with her was a mastery based system which I still don't even know what that means. She is so kind and understanding and is almost always willing to give you second chances on quizzes and give extensions too. She is super accessible outside of class and is holding office hours basically whenever you want to meet.
Amazing
Dr. Cooper is very helpful and friendly. Just go for her if you got any questions. It does not require you to put in lots of effort to get a good grade. Definitely will take her again
Dr. Cooper is great. I have her for Calc 1 and she is awesome. Makes the material very easy to comprehend and is almost impossible to fail this class as long as you do the homework online.
Dr. Cooper is awesome. Highly recommend. Super chill lady and makes class fun.

I took her for Calc 2 and it was a breeze. The grading system is very different and confusing for the first couple of weeks, but once you understand it, you'll also understand how easy it is to do well in the class. Dr. Cooper is really nice and good at explaining concepts and also uses problems similar to ones in class on quizzes.

Dr. Cooper is super sweet and caring. The assignments are doable and you'll likely get perfect scores for them. To ace the exams you basically only need to master the study guides. She's accessible outside class and truly cares about her students so just reach out and you'll do fine. Her lectures are easy to understand. Overall a great teacher.

Taking calc for the gen ed was scary, but having taken AP last year helped a ton. Has helpful guided notes and one homework assignment a week on WebAssign. Be sure to pay attention as she does go semi-quickly and takes the whole class time, but overall a good choice if you want to/have to take calc 1.

Very clear and straightforward teacher whose lectures are truly helpful. Flexible with attendance and posts all possible information needed for the class (including notes, lecture videos, additional resources, and additional problems). Homework is completed virtually but tests/exams are done on paper. A passionate and understanding teacher.
